question: How long will I wait for a decision if I extend my Student visa from inside the UK?
expected: Usually within 8 weeks

citations.title_path: Student visa > Apply online > Apply inside the UK
Student visa > Extend your visa > How long it takes to get a decision

rag.answer: If you extend your Student visa from inside the UK, you will usually get a decision within 8 weeks [1, 5]. You may also be able to pay to get a faster decision [1, 5].

closed_book.answer: If you apply to extend your Student visa from inside the UK, you will usually get a decision within 8 weeks. This 8-week period starts from the date you submit your online application, provided you have attended your biometric appointment or used the UK Immigration: ID Check app.

question: I'm 16. Am I old enough to get a Student visa?
expected: Yes, you can apply from 16, but you need your parents' consent at 16 or 17, and you may be eligible for a Child Student visa instead

citations.title_path: Student visa > Overview

rag.answer: Yes, you can apply for a Student visa to study in the UK if you are 16 or over [1]. If you are 16 or 17, you may also be eligible for a Child Student visa instead [1].

closed_book.answer: Yes, you are old enough to apply for a Student visa at 16 years old. If you are 16 or 17, you will need written consent from your parent or guardian to live and travel independently in the UK. Your parents or guardians must also confirm they agree with your living arrangements and your application.

question: I'm already in the UK on another visa. How early can I apply for my Student visa?
expected: Up to 3 months before the course starts, and before your current visa expires; the new course must start within 28 days of your current visa expiring

citations.title_path: Student visa > Switch to this visa > When to apply

rag.answer: The earliest you can apply for a Student visa is 3 months before your course starts [3]. You must also apply within 6 months of getting a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) [3].

closed_book.answer: You can apply for a Student visa up to 3 months before your course starts if you are applying from inside the UK. Your course must start within 28 days of your current visa expiring, or you must leave the UK and apply from your home country. You must also have received your Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) from your sponsor before applying.

question: How early can I fly to the UK before my course starts?
expected: Up to 1 month before if the course lasts more than 6 months, up to 1 week before if 6 months or less, and never before the start date on your visa

citations.title_path: Student visa > Overview > How long you can stay

rag.answer: You can arrive before your course starts, either up to 1 week before if your course lasts 6 months or less, or up to 1 month before if it lasts more than 6 months [3]. However, you must not travel to the UK before the start date given on your visa, regardless of when your course starts [3].

closed_book.answer: If your course lasts for 6 months or less, you can travel to the UK up to 7 days before your course starts. If your course lasts for longer than 6 months, you can travel up to 1 month before your course starts. These rules apply regardless of the date you apply.

question: How much do I have to pay to apply for a Student visa?
expected: £558, plus the healthcare surcharge

citations.title_path: Student visa > Overview > Fees

rag.answer: It costs £558 to apply for a Student visa from outside the UK, or to extend or switch to a Student visa from inside the UK [1]. You must also pay the healthcare surcharge as part of your application, and the amount depends on how long your visa lasts [1]. Additionally, you must pay the visa fee for each person that joins you [1].

closed_book.answer: To apply for a Student visa from outside the UK, the standard fee is £490 per person. If you are applying to switch to or extend your Student visa from inside the UK, the standard fee is also £490 per person. Additionally, you will need to pay the Immigration Health Surcharge as part of your application.

question: How much money do I need in my bank account to study in Manchester?
expected: £1,171 a month for up to 9 months (outside London), held for at least 28 days in a row, plus the first year's course fees

citations.title_path: Student visa > Money you need > Money to support yourself (‘financial requirement’)
Student visa > Money you need > Course fee

rag.answer: To study in Manchester (outside London), you will need £1,171 per month for up to 9 months to support yourself, unless you have been in the UK with a valid visa for at least 12 months on the date of your application [1]. You also need enough money to pay for your course for 1 academic year (up to 9 months), the amount of which will be on your Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) [5].

closed_book.answer: To study in Manchester, you generally need enough money to cover your course fees for one academic year (up to 9 years) plus living costs. For a course in Manchester, the living costs requirement is £1,024 per month for up to 9 months, meaning you will need a maximum of £9,216 for living costs. You must hold this money in your bank account for at least 2 consecutive consecutive days, ending no more than 31 days before your application date.

question: I'm Canadian. Do I have to take an English test for my Student visa?
expected: No, Canadian nationals do not need to prove their English

citations.title_path: Student visa > Knowledge of English > Passing an English test
Student visa > Knowledge of English > How to prove your knowledge of English

rag.answer: You do not need to take an English test if you can prove your knowledge of English in another way, such as having a UK school qualification, a degree from a UK institution, or a degree from an institution outside the UK that was taught in English [3]. If you do not have any qualifications that prove your knowledge of English, you will need to pass a Secure English Language Test (SELT) from an approved provider [1].

closed_book.answer: As a Canadian citizen, you do not need to prove your knowledge of English through a test when applying for a Student visa, because Canada is recognized by the UK as a majority English-speaking country. Your passport will serve as proof of your nationality.

question: What English level do I need for a Student visa if I'm doing a degree?
expected: CEFR level B2 (B1 for courses below degree level)

citations.title_path: Student visa > Knowledge of English > Passing an English test

rag.answer: If you are studying at degree level or above, you must prove your ability to read, write, speak, and understand English to a level equivalent to CEFR level B2 [3]. Your Higher Education Provider can also assess your level themselves if you are studying at degree level or above [3].

closed_book.answer: If you are studying at or above degree level on a Student visa, you usually need to prove you have CEFR level B2 in reading, writing, speaking, and listening. However, your higher education provider can assess your English language ability themselves using other methods. Therefore, you should check the specific requirements listed in your institution's Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS).

question: My university sent me my CAS 7 months ago. Can I still use it to apply?
expected: No, you must apply within 6 months of receiving your CAS

rag.answer: I can't find this in the gov.uk guidance I have.

closed_book.answer: No, you cannot use a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) that was issued 7 months ago. A CAS is only valid for 6 months from the date it was assigned to you by your university. You will need to request a new CAS from your university before you can apply for your Student visa.

question: Can I do freelance work for my own clients while I'm on a Student visa?
expected: No, you cannot be self-employed on a Student visa

citations.title_path: Student visa > Overview > What you can and cannot do

rag.answer: No, you cannot be self-employed while you are on a Student visa [1].

closed_book.answer: No, you cannot do freelance work or set up a business while on a Student visa. The UK Student visa rules strictly prohibit engaging in business activity, self-employment, or providing freelance services to your own clients. Doing so is a breach of your visa conditions and can result in your visa being curtailed.

question: How long can I stay in the UK with a Graduate visa?
expected: 2 years if you apply on or before 31 December 2026, 18 months if you apply on or after 1 January 2027, or 3 years with a PhD

citations.title_path: Student visa > Overview > How long you can stay
Graduate visa > Overview > How long you can stay

rag.answer: A Graduate visa lasts for 2 years if you apply on or before 31 December 2026, or 18 months if you apply on or after 1 January 2027 [1, 2]. If you have completed a PhD or other doctoral qualification, the visa lasts for 3 years [1, 2].

closed_book.answer: You can stay in the UK for up to 2 years with a Graduate visa. If you have a PhD or other doctoral qualification, you can stay for up to 3 years. This visa cannot be extended, and you must switch to another visa if you want to stay longer.

question: What's the fee for a Graduate visa?
expected: £937, plus the healthcare surcharge (usually £1,035 a year)

citations.title_path: Graduate visa > Overview > How much it costs
Graduate visa > How much it costs

rag.answer: When you apply for a Graduate visa, you must pay a £937 application fee [1, 2]. You also need to pay the healthcare surcharge, which is usually £1,035 for each year you will be in the UK [1, 2].

closed_book.answer: The application fee for a Graduate visa is £822. You must also pay the Immigration Health Surcharge for the full length of your stay, which is £1,035 per year. Both fees must be paid when you submit your application online.

question: Can I extend my Graduate visa when it runs out?
expected: No, it cannot be extended, but you may be able to switch to another visa such as Skilled Worker

citations.title_path: Graduate visa > Overview > How long you can stay

rag.answer: You cannot extend your Graduate visa [1]. However, you may be able to switch to a different visa, such as a Skilled Worker visa [1].

closed_book.answer: No, you cannot extend a Graduate visa. It is a non-extendable visa that allows you to stay in the UK for up to 2 years (or 3 years for a PhD or other doctoral qualification). If you wish to stay in the UK longer, you must switch to a different type of visa, such as a Skilled Worker visa.

question: Do I have to wait for my graduation ceremony before I apply for the Graduate visa?
expected: No, you can apply once your university has told the Home Office you've completed the course, as long as your Student visa hasn't expired

citations.title_path: Graduate visa > Overview > When to apply

rag.answer: No, you do not have to wait until you have graduated or been given a certificate [1]. You can apply after your education provider has told the Home Office that you have successfully completed your course [1].

closed_book.answer: No, you do not have to wait for your graduation ceremony to apply for the Graduate visa. You only need to wait until your UK higher education provider has officially confirmed to the Home Office that you have successfully completed your course.

question: My master's was one year long and I went home over Christmas. Does that still count as studying in the UK for the Graduate visa?
expected: Yes, leaving during term breaks or weekends still counts; you need to have studied in the UK for the full length of a course of 12 months or less

citations.title_path: Graduate visa > The course you studied > How long you studied in the UK for
Graduate visa > Overview > Eligibility

rag.answer: Yes, leaving the UK during term breaks, such as over Christmas, still counts as time spent studying in the UK for a 1-year master's degree [1]. You need to have studied in the UK for at least 12 months if your course's total length is more than 12 months, or the total length of your course if it is shorter [1]. You must also be in the UK when you apply for a Graduate visa [1, 2].

closed_book.answer: Yes, taking authorised holiday or going home during your master's degree still counts as studying in the UK for the Graduate visa. You must have studied your course for at least 12 months (or the full length of your course if it is shorter) while holding a valid student visa. Additionally, you must have been in the UK for the required period of your studies according to the rules in place when you applied.

question: Can I start my own company while I'm on a Graduate visa?
expected: Yes, you can be self-employed on a Graduate visa

citations.title_path: Graduate visa > Overview > What you can and cannot do

rag.answer: Yes, with a Graduate visa you can be self-employed [2].

closed_book.answer: Yes, you can start your own company while on a Graduate visa. The visa allows you to be self-employed and engage in business, provided the business is genuine and meets UK laws. You can also work, do voluntary work, and travel abroad and return to the UK.

question: Can I go home for a holiday while my Graduate visa application is being processed?
expected: No, if you leave the UK, Ireland, the Channel Islands or the Isle of Man before a decision, your application is withdrawn

rag.answer: I can't find this in the gov.uk guidance I have.

closed_book.answer: If you travel outside the UK, Ireland, the Channel Islands, or the Isle of Man while your Graduate visa application is pending, your application will be withdrawn. You must wait until your application has been successfully decided and you have received your visa before you travel abroad. Leaving the Common Travel Area during this time means you will not be able to return on your current student status.

question: What English test score do I need for a Skilled Worker visa?
expected: At least CEFR level B2 (B1 if you had the visa before 8 January 2026 and are extending or updating it)

citations.title_path: Skilled Worker visa > Knowledge of English > Passing an English test

rag.answer: For a Skilled Worker visa, you must generally prove you can read, write, speak, and understand English to at least level B2 on the CEFR scale [1]. However, if you had a Skilled Worker visa before 8 January 2026 and are applying to extend or update it, you need level B1 English [1]. If you are switching from a Health and Care Worker visa, you do not need to provide proof again [1].

closed_book.answer: To qualify for a Skilled Worker visa, you must prove your knowledge of the English language by passing a Secure English Language Test (SELT) from an approved provider. You generally need to achieve at least level B1 on the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) scale in reading, writing, speaking, and listening. You can also meet this requirement if you have a degree taught in English that is equivalent to a UK bachelor's degree or higher, or if you are a national of a majority English-speaking country.

question: How much savings do I need to show for a Skilled Worker visa?
expected: £1,270, held for 28 days in a row, unless you've been in the UK for 12 months or your employer covers your first month's costs

citations.title_path: Skilled Worker visa > How much it costs
Skilled Worker visa > How much it costs > Money to support yourself

rag.answer: You will usually need to have at least £1,270 available in your bank account to support yourself when you arrive in the UK [1, 2]. This money must have been available to you for at least 28 days in a row, with day 28 falling within 31 days of your application [2]. You do not need to show this proof if you have been in the UK with a valid visa for at least 12 months, or if your employer can cover your costs up to £1,270 during your first month [2].

closed_book.answer: You usually need to have at least £1,270 in your bank account to show you can support yourself when applying for a Skilled Worker visa. The money must have been available for at least 30 consecutive days, ending no more than 31 days before you apply. However, you may be exempt from this requirement if you are already in the UK on certain visas or if your employer certifies your maintenance on your Certificate of Sponsorship.

question: If I apply for a Skilled Worker visa from India, how long until I hear back?
expected: Usually within 3 weeks

citations.title_path: Skilled Worker visa > Apply from outside the UK > How long it takes to get a decision

rag.answer: When applying for a Skilled Worker visa from outside the UK, you will usually get a decision within 3 weeks after you have applied online, proved your identity, and provided your documents [1]. You may be able to pay to get a faster decision, and you will be told if this is an option when you apply [1].

closed_book.answer: If you apply for a Skilled Worker visa from outside the UK, including from India, the standard processing time is usually 3 weeks. You may be able to pay for a faster service to get a decision quicker, such as the priority or super priority service, depending on what is available at your visa application centre.

question: Can I have a weekend job on top of my sponsored job?
expected: Yes, up to 20 hours a week if the job meets the conditions (e.g. higher skilled, on the immigration salary list, or same sector and level); more than that needs a visa update

citations.title_path: Skilled Worker visa > Taking on additional work > Working in another job or for your own business
Skilled Worker visa > Update your visa if you change job or employer > Eligibility and documents you’ll need to apply

rag.answer: You can work up to 20 hours a week in another job or for your own business as long as you are still doing your sponsored job, provided the work meets specific conditions [1]. If your second job is more than 20 paid hours a week, you must apply to update your visa to include both jobs [3].

closed_book.answer: Yes, you can usually take a second job (including a weekend job) on top of your sponsored job, provided it meets certain conditions. The secondary job must be on the list of eligible occupations, be at the same skill level as your main sponsored role, and not exceed 20 hours of work per week. Additionally, you must continue to fulfil the duties of your primary sponsored role.

question: A different company offered me a job. Can I just move there on my Skilled Worker visa?
expected: No, you must apply to update your visa first (up to 3 months before the new job starts) and should not start until it's approved

citations.title_path: Skilled Worker visa > Update your visa if you change job or employer

rag.answer: You will need to apply to update your Skilled Worker visa if you change your job and your new job is with a different employer [1]. Your partner or children will also need to apply separately to update their visas [1].

closed_book.answer: No, you cannot just move to a new employer on your current Skilled Worker visa. Your new employer must be a Home Office-approved sponsor and provide you with a new Certificate of Sponsorship (CoS). You must then submit a new visa application to update your visa with your new job details before you can start working for them.

question: After how many years on a Skilled Worker visa can I get permanent residency?
expected: After 5 years you may be able to apply for indefinite leave to remain

citations.title_path: Skilled Worker visa > Overview > How long you can stay

rag.answer: After 5 years on a Skilled Worker visa, you may be able to apply to settle permanently in the UK, which is also known as 'indefinite leave to remain' [1].

closed_book.answer: You can usually apply for permanent residency (known as settlement or Indefinite Leave to Remain) after living and working in the UK for 5 continuous years on a Skilled Worker visa. You must also continue to meet the salary requirements and other eligibility criteria at the time of your application. Time spent on certain other visa categories may also count towards this 5-year qualifying period.

question: How much money does my wife need to show to join me on my Skilled Worker visa?
expected: £285 for a partner, held for 28 days in a row

citations.title_path: Skilled Worker visa > Your partner and children > Money they need to support themselves

rag.answer: To bring your partner to the UK, you, your partner, or your child will need to have £285 available for your partner [3]. This money must have been available for at least 28 days in a row, with day 28 falling within 31 days of applying for the visa [3]. You usually need to show proof of this unless you have all been in the UK with a valid visa for at least 12 months, or your employer can cover your family's costs during their first month [3].

closed_book.answer: To bring your wife to the UK as your dependant on a Skilled Worker visa, she generally needs to show £285 for her own funds. You will also need to show additional funds for any other dependants joining you (£315 for the first child and £200 for each additional child). These funds usually need to be held in a bank account for a consecutive 28-day period ending no more than 31 days before the date of application. However, you and your partner may be exempt from this financial requirement if you have already been in the UK with a valid visa for at least 12 months, or if your sponsor has certified your maintenance on the Certificate of Sponsorship.

question: I'm starting a one-year taught master's in September. Can my wife come with me?
expected: Usually no: postgraduate courses starting on or after 1 January 2024 must be a PhD or research degree, unless you're a government-sponsored student on a course longer than 6 months

rag.answer: I can't find this in the gov.uk guidance I have.

closed_book.answer:
As a general rule, dependents (like a wife) can only join a student on a UK visa if the student is on a postgraduate level course that lasts for 9 months or more, *and* is either a PhD or other doctorate (RQF level 8) or a research-based higher degree. Because your course is a *taught* master's degree, you will not be permitted to bring dependents.

question: What's the minimum salary I need to get a Skilled Worker visa?
expected: £41,700 a year or the going rate for the job, whichever is higher (lower in some cases)

citations.title_path: Skilled Worker visa > Your job
Skilled Worker visa > Your job > Salary requirements
Skilled Worker visa > When you can be paid less

rag.answer: To be eligible for a Skilled Worker visa, you must usually be paid at least £41,700 per year or the 'going rate' for your job, whichever is higher [1, 2]. However, the minimum salary may be lower if you are extending your visa, updating it due to a new job or employer, switching to become a prison officer, or if you meet specific criteria that allow you to be paid less (such as being under 26, a recent graduate, or having a relevant PhD) [1, 2, 3].

closed_book.answer: To get a Skilled Worker visa, you generally need to meet the general salary threshold of £38,700 per year, or the specific "going rate" for your occupation, whichever is higher. However, you may be able to be paid less (known as a "going rate discount") if you qualify under certain rules, such as having a PhD relevant to your job, working in a shortage occupation, or being a new entrant to the job market.

question: If I apply for my Graduate visa in February 2027, how long will it last?
expected: 18 months (3 years with a PhD)

citations.title_path: Graduate visa > Overview > How long you can stay

rag.answer: If you apply for a Graduate visa on or after 1 January 2027, it will last for 18 months [1]. However, if you have a PhD or other doctoral qualification, the visa will last for 3 years [1].

closed_book.answer: If you apply for a Graduate visa, it will typically last for 2 years. However, if your eligible qualification is a PhD or other doctoral qualification, the visa will last for 3 years.

question: I'm on a Graduate visa. Can a company sponsor me for a Skilled Worker job that pays less than the normal minimum?
expected: Yes, you can be paid 70% of the going rate if it's at least £33,400 a year, but your total stay (including Graduate visa time) cannot exceed 4 years

citations.title_path: Skilled Worker visa > When you can be paid less > You’re under 26, studying or a recent graduate, or in professional training

rag.answer: You may be able to apply for a Skilled Worker visa with a lower salary if you are currently in the UK on a Graduate visa (or have been in the last 2 years, provided a Graduate or visit visa was your most recent visa) [3]. To qualify under this category, your salary must be at least £33,400 per year, which allows you to be paid 70% of your job's standard going rate [3]. Additionally, your total stay in the UK cannot exceed 4 years, which includes any time already spent on a Graduate visa [3].

closed_book.answer: Yes, a company can sponsor you for a Skilled Worker visa if your job pays less than the standard minimum, provided you meet certain criteria. For example, you may qualify for a "new entrant" discount if you are under 26, studying, or recently graduated. Alternatively, your salary could be lower if the job is on the Immigration Salary List or if you have a relevant PhD.

question: What will a 2-year Skilled Worker visa cost me in total if I apply from abroad?
expected: £819 application fee plus £1,035 a year healthcare surcharge, £2,889 in total, plus £1,270 savings unless your employer covers it (lower fee if the job is on the immigration salary list)

citations.title_path: Skilled Worker visa > How much it costs

rag.answer: If you are applying to come to the UK from abroad for a Skilled Worker visa for 2 years and your job is not on the immigration salary list, the standard application fee is £819 [1]. You will also need to pay the healthcare surcharge, which is usually £1,035 for each year of your stay [1]. This brings the total cost to £2,889, and you will also need to prove you have £1,270 available to support yourself unless your employer can cover these costs [1].

closed_book.answer: I can't find this in the gov.uk guidance I have.

question: Can I switch from my Student visa to a Skilled Worker visa before I finish my course?
expected: Only if your job starts after the course ends, or you're a full-time PhD student who has studied for at least 24 months; otherwise you must complete the course first

rag.answer: I can't find this in the gov.uk guidance I have.

closed_book.answer: Yes, you can switch from a Student visa to a Skilled Worker visa before you finish your course, provided certain conditions are met. You must have successfully completed your course, or you can switch up to 3 months before your course end date if your employer's job start date is after that end date. For PhD students, you can switch after you have completed at least 24 months of your studies in the UK. Your sponsoring employer must also be a licensed sponsor and issue you a valid Certificate of Sponsorship.

question: I'm from Malaysia. Do I need to show bank statements for my Student visa?
expected: Usually not, Malaysia is on the differential evidence list, but you might still be asked for it before a decision

citations.title_path: Student visa > Money you need > When you do not need to prove you have money to support yourself

rag.answer: You do not need to prove you have enough money to support yourself if you are from Malaysia, as it is listed under the differential evidence requirement [1]. However, you might still be asked to provide this evidence before you get a decision on your application [1]. If UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) requires this, they will contact you after you have submitted your application [1].

closed_book.answer: As a national of Malaysia, you generally do not need to submit your bank statements or evidence of qualifications with your Student visa application, as Malaysia is included in the differential evidence requirement list. However, UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) still expects you to meet the financial requirements and can request these documents at any time during the decision-making process. Therefore, you must ensure you still hold the required funds in case you are asked to provide proof.

question: Can I apply for British citizenship straight after my Graduate visa?
expected: Not covered by these guides

rag.answer: I can't find this in the gov.uk guidance I have.

closed_book.answer: No, you cannot apply for British citizenship straight after a Graduate visa because the time spent on a Graduate route does not count towards the continuous residence requirement for naturalisation. To apply for citizenship, you must first switch to a visa that leads to settlement, such as a Skilled Worker visa, and typically hold indefinite leave to remain (settled status) for a period before applying.

question: How many hours a week can I work during term time on a Student visa?
expected: Not covered: the guides only say it depends on the course and whether it's term time, without giving a number

rag.answer: I can't find this in the gov.uk guidance I have.

closed_book.answer: If you are studying a full-time degree-level course (or above) at a sponsor with a track record of compliance, you can usually work up to 20 hours a week during term time. For courses below degree level, or at institutions without this status, the limit is usually 10 hours a week during term time. The exact number of hours you are permitted to work will be stated on your immigration permission (visa vignette or biometric residence permit).

question: How do my parents apply for a visitor visa to come to my graduation?
expected: Not covered by these guides

rag.answer: I can't find this in the gov.uk guidance I have.

closed_book.answer: Your parents must apply online for a Standard Visitor visa from outside the UK before they travel. They will need to complete the online application form, pay the visa fee, and book an appointment at a visa application centre to submit their fingerprints and photograph. As supporting documents, they should include a formal graduation invitation letter from your university, proof of your status in the UK, and evidence that they can afford their trip and will leave after the graduation.

question: How do I get a National Insurance number?
expected: Not covered by these guides

rag.answer: I can't find this in the gov.uk guidance I have.

closed_book.answer: To get a National Insurance number, you must usually live and work in the UK, and have the right to work here. You can apply online through the GOV.UK website by proving your identity with documents like your passport or biometric residence permit. Once your application is submitted, you will receive your National Insurance number by post.
